expected_legend.fix-T0: Mechanical change with no runtime semantics (comments, dead text, docs). Expected in the diff.
expected_legend.fix-T1: Local, unambiguous code fix that preserves behaviour on valid inputs or restores behaviour the code's own contract already promises. Expected in the diff, verified by tests.
expected_legend.report-T2: Changes reported numbers or outputs, needs a policy decision, or is a broad refactor. Expected in the report with a proposed fix; an unapproved fix is acceptable only if flagged as behaviour-changing and the hidden tests still pass.

defects.description: Public-looking helper open_symbols() is referenced nowhere: not by src, tests, README, config, or tradelog.__all__.
defects.detection_hint: Reference search for 'open_symbols' finds only the definition; no getattr/string lookup of it exists. Contrast with the X02/X03 traps, which do have dynamic or documented consumers.

defects.description: Module csvutil (sniff_dialect, normalize_header, iter_rows) is never imported. fills.py stopped using it in 'feat(fills): normalise venue dialects'; it is also missing from the README layout.
defects.detection_hint: No import of tradelog.csvutil and no string reference to 'csvutil' anywhere; git log -p src/tradelog/fills.py shows the import being dropped.

defects.description: python-dateutil is a declared runtime dependency but nothing imports dateutil since 'refactor(timeutil): parse timestamps with fromisoformat instead of dateutil'. The README even claims 'standard library only at runtime'.
defects.detection_hint: grep for 'dateutil' in src/ and tests/ returns nothing; deptry-style check of declared vs imported packages.

defects.anchor: # slippage model from the first version, kept for reference
defects.description: Seven lines of commented-out slippage code left inside the exit branch of run_backtest after 'refactor(backtest): drop the slippage model'. The history already keeps the old version.
defects.detection_hint: Comment block that parses as Python (eradicate / ERA001).

defects.description: _trade_fee duplicates fees.fee_for_notional but never received the abs() fix from 'fix(fees): charge fees on the absolute notional'. Short entries and exits (negative qty) get negative fees, i.e. fees are credited, inflating every short-side backtest (e.g. the mean_revert config shows negative 'fees' on sell trades).
defects.detection_hint: Compare with src/tradelog/fees.py:50 ('abs(notional)'); git show of the fees fix touches only fees.py; tradelog backtest --config examples/config.toml --json prints negative fees on 'sell' trades.

defects.description: _normalize_row is a 68-line function with nesting depth 5 and cyclomatic complexity around 25 (16 if/elif decision points plus 'or' chains), mixing side/qty normalisation, fee parsing, fee-currency inference and venue defaults, returning an untyped dict[str, object].
defects.detection_hint: Cyclomatic complexity well above 10 (ruff C901 / radon); split into _side_and_qty, _fee, _fee_currency helpers pinned by characterisation tests.

defects.description: parse_fills silently drops any row that fails to parse (bad number, unknown side, negative sell qty, bad timestamp, missing price) with a bare 'continue': no log, no count, no way for the caller to know fills were lost. The module logger exists but is not used here.
defects.detection_hint: except clause whose body is only 'continue'; log is defined at module level but not used in the handler. Keep the skip semantics, add a warning with the row number (or a skipped-rows count).

defects.description: PricePoller._notify swallows every listener exception with 'except Exception: pass', so a broken listener fails silently forever.
defects.detection_hint: except Exception: pass (ruff S110 / SIM105-style); replace with log.exception and keep notifying the other listeners.

defects.description: On any fetch failure _fetch fabricates a Quote: the last good price re-stamped with the current time, or price 0.0 if none. Listeners and the CLI print it as a fresh, real quote; only the errors counter hints at the failure.
defects.detection_hint: Broad except returning a value shaped like success; stale price with a fresh timestamp, 0.0 as a price.

defects.description: _load_marks returns {} when the marks file is missing, unreadable or malformed, so 'tradelog pnl --marks typo.json' exits 0 and reports unrealized PnL of 0 as if every position were marked at cost.
defects.detection_hint: Error handler returning an empty result for a user-supplied path; compare with load_fills, whose errors reach main() and exit 2.

defects.description: HttpFetcher calls urlopen without a timeout; a stalled connection blocks the worker thread and the poller forever (asyncio.to_thread cannot be cancelled).
defects.detection_hint: urlopen/requests call without timeout= (bandit S113-style); make the timeout a constructor parameter with a default.

defects.description: Fees are binary floats rounded with round(x, 2): half-even on an inexact binary value (e.g. 0.125 -> 0.12, 2.675 -> 2.67) and sub-cent fees on small crypto fills round to 0.00. Money is float throughout (Fill.fee/price, Position totals).
defects.detection_hint: round() on a money float; no Decimal/quantize anywhere; estimate_fee on a $4 fill at 10 bps returns 0.0.

defects.description: Epoch timestamps are converted with datetime.fromtimestamp() without tz, i.e. to naive LOCAL time, while the module contract (and the ISO branch) is naive UTC. On a non-UTC machine epoch-stamped fills are shifted (examples/fills.csv row f-1006 shows 14:00 instead of 12:00 in Paris).
defects.detection_hint: fromtimestamp without tz= (ruff DTZ006); module docstring says UTC.

defects.description: action_counts mutates its default dict, so counts accumulate across calls in the same process (a second journal in a library session or test double-counts).
defects.detection_hint: ruff B006; the default dict is written to inside the function.

defects.description: Fire-and-forget create_task without keeping a reference: the event loop only holds a weak reference, so the task can be garbage-collected mid-flight, and its exceptions are never retrieved.
defects.detection_hint: ruff RUF006 (asyncio-dangling-task); keep tasks in a set with add_done_callback(discard) or await the notification.

defects.description: Public run_backtest validates its argument with assert; under python -O the check disappears and a zero/negative cash produces a ZeroDivisionError or nonsense results.
defects.detection_hint: bandit B101 / ruff S101 on an argument check in a public function; replace with ValueError (exception type changes).

defects.description: PricePoller.run returns from inside finally, which swallows any in-flight exception, including asyncio.CancelledError and KeyboardInterrupt: cancelling the poller task silently returns a round count instead of cancelling.
defects.detection_hint: ruff B012 / PEP 765 (SyntaxWarning in Python 3.14); move the return after the try/finally.

defects.description: Five bare '# type: ignore' comments (no error code, no reason) hide that _normalize_row returns dict[str, object], so the Fill fields are untyped.
defects.detection_hint: Bare type: ignore (mypy warn_unused_ignores / ruff PGH003); return a typed NamedTuple/dataclass from the normaliser instead. Contrast with cli.py:148, which carries an error code and a comment.

defects.description: PricePoller.history keeps every quote ever fetched (appended at line 64, never trimmed or read) in a process designed to run forever, so memory grows without bound.
defects.detection_hint: Append-only per-instance list in a long-running loop; bound it with deque(maxlen=...) (configurable) or drop it, since nothing reads it.

defects.anchor: if fill.fill_id in [f.fill_id for f in fills]:
defects.description: Duplicate detection rebuilds a list of all seen ids for every row: O(n^2) in the number of fills (a 100k-row export performs ~5e9 comparisons).
defects.detection_hint: Membership test against a list comprehension inside a loop; use a set of seen ids (first occurrence still wins).

defects.anchor: method from the previous session, as requested
defects.description: Comment narrates the agent's conversation ('Updated per review ... from the previous session, as requested') instead of explaining the code; the surrounding 'Step N' comments are also narration.
defects.detection_hint: Comment words: 'as requested', 'previous session', 'Updated per review'.

defects.description: README still shows --strategy-params, which 'refactor(cli): replace --strategy-params with a repeatable --param' removed; the command fails with 'unrecognized arguments'. Correct form: --param fast=5 --param slow=20.
defects.detection_hint: Run the README commands; compare with build_parser() in cli.py and the updated tests/test_cli.py.

defects.anchor: # TODO: compute peak-to-trough drawdown from equity_curve
defects.description: max_drawdown is a TODO stub that always returns 0.0, yet it is printed by the CLI ('max drawdown 0.00%') and serialised in the JSON contract as if it were measured.
defects.detection_hint: TODO plus constant return in a property exposed in to_dict() and CLI output.

defects.description: test_backtest_json_roundtrip asserts nothing: it only checks that json.dumps/json.loads do not raise, so the JSON contract (schema_version, trade_count, keys) is untested by the visible suite.
defects.detection_hint: Test function without assert/pytest.raises; mutation of to_dict() survives the visible suite.

defects.description: An API key literal is committed in source and used as the default X-API-Key header of every HttpFetcher. (The value is a clearly fake fixture string.)
defects.detection_hint: Secret-looking literal (sk_...) assigned to API_KEY (gitleaks / bandit B105); read it from an environment variable, and note that the key would need rotating if it were real.

traps.description: Module and class are imported nowhere in src or tests and are not registered in the strategy registry, so it looks like an unused file.
traps.why_required: It is loaded by string reference 'tradelog.strategies.mean_revert:MeanReversion' from examples/config.toml (and the README) through plugins.import_object / strategies.get_strategy.

traps.description: render_text, render_json and render_csv are never called by name anywhere, so a reference search reports them as unused.
traps.why_required: get_renderer() resolves them with getattr(sys.modules[__name__], f'render_{fmt}') for 'tradelog pnl --format text|json|csv' (line 27).

traps.description: effective_fee_rate is not called anywhere inside the package or the visible tests; its only internal reference is the re-export in tradelog/__init__.py.
traps.why_required: It is part of the documented library API: exported in tradelog.__all__ and used in the README 'Library usage' example for external consumers.

traps.description: schedule_for silently falls back to DEFAULT_SCHEDULE for unknown venues, which pattern-matches 'success-shaped fallback'.
traps.why_required: The fallback is documented (comment at lines 27-29, docstring, README 'Fees') and deliberately conservative (the most expensive schedule); estimate_fee and the journal depend on unknown venues not raising.

traps.anchor: from tradelog.strategies import momentum, sma_cross  # noqa: E402,F401
traps.description: Late import of momentum and sma_cross whose names are never used, silenced with noqa F401/E402; looks like an unused import to remove or hoist.
traps.why_required: Importing those modules runs their @register_strategy decorators; without it the registry is empty in a fresh interpreter ('tradelog strategies' prints nothing, 'sma_cross' is unknown).

traps.description: SCHEMA_VERSION / 'schema_version' (and the redundant 'trade_count') are written to the JSON payload but never read anywhere in the code.
traps.why_required: They are part of the documented JSON output contract of 'tradelog backtest --json' (README 'JSON output'); downstream consumers key on schema_version.

traps.description: The 'case _: raise ValueError' arm of the match on Side looks unreachable because Side has only BUY and SELL.
traps.why_required: It guards future Side variants and malformed fills: without it signed_qty is unbound and apply_fill fails with UnboundLocalError instead of a clear ValueError.

traps.description: poll_once awaits each symbol's fetch one after another (with request_spacing sleeps), an obvious-looking asyncio.gather optimisation target.
traps.why_required: The ticker endpoint rate-limits bursts per IP (comment at lines 56-58, README 'Live poller'); requests must stay sequential, ordered and spaced.
